 th Order No. 05/Dated: 14 August, 2024  IA No. 6009 of 2024 Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the State on the Interlocutory Application filed on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence, during pendency of the criminal appeal.

The present appeal is directed against the judgment of conviction dated 22-04-2024 and order of sentence dated 27-04-2024, passed by the Additional Judicial Commissioner-IV-cum-Special Judge, POCSO-cum- Children Court, Ranchi in Children Case No.03/2022 (arising out of Sadar P.S.
Case No.224/2020), whereby and where under, the learned trial Court has convicted the appellant under section 376/511 and 342 of IPC and section 4/18 of the POCSO Act and sentenced him to undergo RI for 7 years, under section 4 read with section 18 of the POCSO Act, and also awarded fine of Rs. 10,000/- upon him.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Commissioner-IV-cum-Special Judge, POCSO-cum- Children Court, Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In default of payment of fine he was further directed to undergo SI for 6 month separately.
He is further sentence to undergo RI for 1 year under section 342 of IPC.

The learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that during trial the appellant has remained in custody for about 3 years, 10 months and 18 days and by now he has spent another four months in custody which would be approximately 4 years 2 months, therefore, the appellant has spent half of the imposed sentence of 7 years.

He has further stated that PW-5 who is the doctor has stated that she has not found any sign of sexual intercourse and not found any injury over the body of the Raj Munda @ Raj Kumar Munda @ Raj Nayak vs The State Of Jharkhand on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33164793/
1 victim.

sentences.text: The learned counsel has further pointed out Exts. 5 and 6 and submitted that no semen was found and as per PW-6 who is Dr. V.K. Yadav has found blood positive and semen negative frock cuttings marked A-I, blood and semen negative leggings cutting marked A-2, Swab of blood and semen negative glass light marked B1, semen negative underwear cutting marked B2 and semen negative public hair marked B3.
The learned counsel for the appellant has further stated that this is not a case under section 376 IPC rather under 376/511 IPC.
Therefore, based on the aforesaid circumstances and period of detention, the benefit of suspension of sentence may be granted to the appellant.

The learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and submitted that offence under section 376/511 IPC is fully made out and the victim has fully supported the case of prosecution .
He has further stated that in the impugned judgment the learned court below has observed that till completion of 21 years of age, the appellant be kept in a place of safety home at Simdega.

Having heard learned counsels for the parties and in the facts and circumstances of the case and the period of custody spent by the appellant, the appellant is ordered to be released on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner, IV cum Spl. Jduge POCSO -cum- Children Court, Ranchi in connection with Children Case No 03 of 2022, arising out of Sadar PS Case No. 224 of 2020, subject to the condition that the appellant shall submit self-attested photocopy of his Aadhar Card and mobile number before the learned court below which he will always keep active and will not change it during pendency of the case without prior permission of the Court.
IA No. 6009 of 2024 stands allowed and disposed of.

(Ratnaker Bhengra, J.) KNR Raj Munda @ Raj Kumar Munda @ Raj Nayak vs The State Of Jharkhand on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33164793/
